wcag_checklist.notes: Body text color #0f172a on #ffffff yields a 15.8:1 contrast ratio (exceeds 4.5:1 requirement). Dark theme text #f8fafc on #131c31 yields 15.2:1. Muted text #334155 yields 7.2:1.
A high-contrast .skip-link is the first focusable element on every page, jumping focus directly to #main-content when pressed.

Proper semantic landmarks used throughout (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <footer>). Exactly one <h1> per page with strictly descending heading levels (h1 → h2 → h3). Tables include <caption> and <th scope="col/row">.
100% of links, buttons, theme toggles, mobile menus, table sort headers, and quiz form radio buttons can be operated exclusively via Tab, Shift+Tab, Space, and Enter.
High-visibility focus indicator implemented: :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent-focus); outline-offset: 3px; }. Never suppressed.
No information is conveyed by color alone. Badges for Free, Freemium, and Paid use clear text words and distinct border stylings. Links have persistent underline styling.
Layout tested at 200% browser zoom in Chrome and Firefox. All typography uses relative rem units. No horizontal scrollbars or clipped text containers.
Zero generic 'click here' or 'read more' links. Every link text describes the destination (e.g., 'Read Complete Guide 1 →', 'Visit Official Website'). Outbound links include screen reader notices.
Includes complete @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) CSS rule disabling transitions and animations for users with vestibular sensitivities.
Every informative SVG illustration contains meaningful descriptive alt text and captions. Decorative icons use aria-hidden="true".

student_feedback.name: Participant 1
student_feedback.task_assigned: Complete Setup Guide 1 (LeechBlock NG + Focus Sessions) and attempt to bypass during study time.
student_feedback.quote: The 64-character uncheatable challenge code is brilliant. I tried opening YouTube to look up a gaming clip while compiling code, saw the random character string, and realized it would take me 45 seconds to type it out. It completely snapped me out of my impulse loop.
student_feedback.problem_encountered: P1 was initially unsure how to whitelist their college's NPTEL lecture playlist on LeechBlock.

student_feedback.name: Participant 2
student_feedback.task_assigned: Follow Guide 2 (Android Bedtime Mode & Grayscale Automation).
student_feedback.quote: Turning the screen black and white at 11 PM makes Instagram reels feel completely uninteresting. After 3 minutes, my eyes feel tired and I just plug the phone in and go to sleep. I was worried about missing my mother's calls, but the starred contacts bypass worked perfectly.
student_feedback.problem_encountered: The aggressive battery saver on MIUI initially delayed Bedtime Mode by 15 minutes.

student_feedback.name: Participant 3
student_feedback.task_assigned: Take the Find My Tool Quiz with a ₹0 budget and evaluate recommendations.
student_feedback.quote: I liked that the quiz didn't push me to download apps with 7-day trials that charge money later. It recommended LeechBlock NG and Android Digital Wellbeing and explicitly told me what features Cold Turkey paywalls.
student_feedback.problem_encountered: P3 wanted a one-click button on the quiz results card to jump straight into the setup guide.

student_feedback.name: Participant 4
student_feedback.task_assigned: Follow Guide 3 (uBlock Origin YouTube Shorts Removal).
student_feedback.quote: Shorts was my biggest weakness. I’d open YouTube to watch a surveying tutorial and end up watching 40 minutes of vertical comedy reels. Removing the Shorts shelf entirely makes YouTube feel like a quiet library again.
student_feedback.problem_encountered: Initially pasted the cosmetic rules without clicking 'Apply changes'.

student_feedback.name: Participant 5
student_feedback.task_assigned: Security audit of the Privacy & Safety section and Compare matrix.
student_feedback.quote: It's refreshing to see a student hub honestly explain Android Accessibility Service risks instead of just telling people to install random blockers. Highlighting Bitwarden and local-first ActivityWatch makes this a genuine wellness resource.
student_feedback.problem_encountered: Requested clear keyboard outline visibility for dark mode buttons.

revisions_log.fix_implemented: Added explicit instructions and code snippet in Guide 1, Step 2 explaining how to use +youtube.com/playlist?list=... syntax to whitelist professor playlists while keeping the algorithmic homepage blocked.
Added dedicated troubleshooting item in Guide 2 Common Problems explaining how to set Digital Wellbeing battery management to 'Unrestricted' in budget Chinese Android skins.
Updated js/main.js recommendation engine so that matched tools automatically render a high-priority 'Read Student Setup Guide' button directly linking to Guide 1, 2, or 3.
Added bold visual callout and diagram notation in Guide 3, Step 3 highlighting the orange 'Apply changes' button so users do not close the tab before saving filter rules.

Implemented dual-view responsive design: on viewports under 840px, the complex 10-column comparison table automatically collapses into accessible, standalone semantic cards (.tool-mobile-card) with zero horizontal scroll clipping.
Added dynamic aria-sort="ascending" / aria-sort="descending" updates to table column headers in js/main.js and added explicit aria-live="polite" regions.
